transcript.text: indesit oven stoped heating, fan goes round n light on but its stone cold after 20 mins. grill werks fine tho. any ideas b4 i call some1 out

Most likely: the main oven heating element has failed.

On many Indesit fan ovens, the fan and light can still work normally even when the circular heating element behind the rear panel has gone open-circuit. The grill being OK usually means the cooker has power and points away from a general supply fault.

Before calling someone out, check:

1. Correct function selected
   Make sure it’s on fan oven / conventional oven, not fan-only or defrost (fan-only deliberately blows unheated air).

2. Clock/timer set to manual
   Some Indesit ovens will not heat if the clock is flashing or the programmer is set to Auto. Set the time and select the “hand/manual” symbol if yours has one.

3. Temperature setting
   Try fan oven at 200°C, leave it 10 minutes, and carefully see if there is any warmth from the air. If completely cold, element is very likely.

4. Look at the rear element — power isolated first
   Switch it off at the cooker isolation switch / unplug it, then remove the oven shelves and inspect the circular element around the fan at the back. Signs include:
• a split, crack, blister or burn mark
• part of the element looking swollen or rough
• sometimes it looks normal despite being faulty

5. Did it trip the electrics when it failed?
   If an RCD/fuse tripped around the time it stopped heating, that makes a failed element even more likely.

If you have a multimeter and are competent working around appliances, the element can be tested for continuity/resistance with the cooker fully isolated. A healthy element commonly reads roughly 20–50 ohms; an open/infinite reading means it has failed. Don’t test it live.

Other possible faults are the oven thermostat, selector switch, thermal cut-out, or control board/relay, but with “fan runs, light works, grill works, oven stone cold”, the fan-oven element is the usual culprit.

Replacing an element is often a fairly routine repair, but it involves removing panels and wiring at mains voltage, so call an appliance engineer if you’re not fully confident. Have the full model number from the door frame/rating plate ready — it will look something like `ID...` or `FI...`.

ok tried a few of those. clock is on manual, nothing flashing, and nothing tripped. its hardwired thru a switch on the wall so i isolated that, took the back panel off and theres a blister/split in the element near the bottom with a black mark. no multimeter tho. so is it the element then?

Yes — that blister/split and black mark is conclusive enough: the fan-oven element has failed.

It explains exactly what you’re seeing: fan and lamp work, grill works, but fan-oven mode blows cold air. The element has physically burnt through/open-circuited.

Don’t use the oven heating function again until it’s replaced. Leave it isolated before touching anything inside.

You have two realistic options:

• Appliance engineer: straightforward job, usually around 30–60 minutes plus the part.
• DIY replacement: possible if you’re confident, but only with the cooker fully isolated at the wall switch and ideally its circuit confirmed dead. Elements are usually held by a couple of screws inside the oven, with wires connected behind the rear casing. Take clear photos of every connection before removing anything.

To order the correct part, use the full model number from the rating label — commonly around the oven door frame, behind/under the door, side trim, or sometimes on the rear. Search for:

`Indesit [full model number] fan oven element`

Avoid ordering purely by appearance or wattage; several similar-looking elements have different fittings and shapes.

One caution: if the element screws are corroded or the wire terminals are burnt/loose, stop and get an engineer. Also, elements can occasionally fail because of a connection or control fault, but a visibly split element itself definitely needs replacing.
